component.name: Backtrack
component.summary: Browse your files as they were

description.p: Backtrack keeps your files backed up and lets you move back through time to bring back what you lost. Pick a folder, step back to this morning or last week, and restore a file without needing to know how backups work.

ul.li: Automatic backups to a drive, a network share or a server over SSH
Changes kept safe on this computer while the backup drive is away
Search across every backup, including files deleted since
Compare a file with an earlier version before restoring it
Restore Previous Version from Nautilus and Dolphin
Restore everything onto a new computer

description.p: Backtrack is built on Borg Backup: backups are encrypted, deduplicated, and readable with Borg itself.

screenshot.caption: A folder as it was at an earlier backup
The same window in the dark style
Restore Previous Version from the file manager

ul.li: Automatic, encrypted, deduplicated backups with Borg, to an external drive, a network folder or an SSH server: hourly by default, or daily, weekly or by hand. A computer that was asleep catches up when it wakes, and backups wait while on battery or a metered connection unless you say otherwise. A welcome wizard sets it all up, with a recovery key to save or print, or opens backups you already have.

Protection away from the backup destination: the files you change are kept on this computer, small and encrypted, as snapshots you can browse like backups, and sent on as soon as the destination is back.

A window for going back in time: the folder stays where it is while you step through its backups, grouped by today, yesterday, this week and earlier months, listing only those in which the folder changed. Files are marked "deleted" or "changed"; a calendar, a strip of the whole history and a jump to a file's next change move further; a preview shows the file as it was. Everything is read from a catalogue on this computer, so it is instant and works with the destination unplugged.

Rewind, a full-screen view of a folder's history: the folder as it is now in front, its backups receding behind it over your desktop's wallpaper, and a timeline down the side. Open it from the window (Ctrl+T), the file manager, the launcher or the tray.

Restores that ask only what matters: which of two versions is newer, one summary for a folder with a file-by-file review if you want it, and nothing ever deleted. Undo stays offered after a restore, and every file a restore replaces is kept for 30 days in Recently Replaced Files. Restore To… puts files in a folder of your choice instead.
Search across every backup (Ctrl+F), with what is missing from your computer first and where and when each file existed, and Compare with Today for text, images and other files.

What you move to the Trash appears in the timeline until the Trash is emptied, so a file made and deleted between two backups can still be got back. On btrfs, Snapper's snapshots appear too, and Preferences can set Snapper up on Fedora, openSUSE and Arch Linux.
Restoring a whole computer onto a new one: everything, or the folders you choose, a folder at a time, paused and resumed at will, never overwriting a file on the new computer without asking.

Backtrack says when your backups need you, and only then: a banner and a notification after a day without a backup or when backups have stopped, each with a Fix… for the problem. A monthly check for damage runs in the background.
Preferences with every setting on five pages, applied as you change them, including the passphrase, the recovery key, checking and repairing the backups, and running the wizard again.

Right-click items in GNOME Files and Dolphin (Restore Previous Version…, Browse Backups of This Folder…, Rewind This File…, Rewind This Folder…), a tray icon on desktops with a tray, and the backtrack command for status, backups, search and restores from a terminal.
Accessible throughout: a screen reader can follow the window and Rewind, everything works from the keyboard, and high contrast is honoured.
Packages for Fedora (COPR), Ubuntu (PPA) and Arch Linux (AUR), and a Flatpak on FriendlyHub, for x86_64 and 64-bit ARM.
Guides to Rewind, the Trash, Snapper and the file manager items.
